subject: Food Science
title: The Jungle and the FDA
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Jungle and the FDA.

hook.text: Upton Sinclair's 1906 novel 'The Jungle' exposed rat-infested meatpacking plants.

buildup.text: Sinclair described workers falling into rendering vats, diseased cattle processed for consumption, and chemical preservatives.

discovery.text: President Theodore Roosevelt sent investigators who confirmed Sinclair's claims.

twist.text: Sinclair wrote the book to expose worker exploitation, not food safety. He said: 'I aimed at the public's heart, and by accident.

climax.text: The FDA now regulates 80% of the US food supply. One novel—written about labor, not food.

punchline.text: A novel about workers created food safety law. One book, two laws, and the FDA was born.

quiz.question: What was Upton Sinclair's actual intent in writing 'The Jungle'?
options: To expose worker exploitation—food safety reform was an unintended consequence
